reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No direct PD-1 occupancy data provided, but pembrolizumab is a well-established PD-1 inhibitor with known pharmacology at 200mg q3w dosing. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Limited biomarker evidence - PET SUV reduction of -1 (95% CI: -7 to 2) suggests some metabolic changes but confidence interval crosses zero. Safety profile shows immune-related adverse events (hyperthyroidism, colitis, hepatitis) consistent with PD-1 pathway activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with 24% pathologic response rate and median tumor size reduction of -4.0mm (95% CI: -13.5 to 0.0). This demonstrates clinical activity in neoadjuvant NSCLC setting. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported in this single-arm study of 30 patients. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design limits interpretation, small sample size, but appropriate neoadjuvant timeframe for assessment.

failure_modes.evidence: 24% pathologic response rate suggests only a subset of patients responded, though this is expected for checkpoint inhibitors and considered clinically meaningful
